questions.q: Find the total area between $f(x) = \sin x$ and the $x$-axis on $[0, 2\pi]$ (note the curve is below the axis on part of this interval).
questions.target: Setting up with respect to y, and total area
questions.answer: By symmetry, $\int_0^\pi \sin x\,dx = 2$ and $\left|\int_\pi^{2\pi}\sin x\,dx\right| = 2$. Total area $= 2 + 2 = 4$.
questions.explanation: By symmetry, $\int_0^\pi \sin x\,dx = 2$ and $\left|\int_\pi^{2\pi}\sin x\,dx\right| = 2$. Total area $= 2 + 2 = 4$.

questions.q: Find the area of the region bounded by $y=x^2-4$ and $y=4-x^2$.
questions.target: More area problems
questions.answer: Intersections: $x^2-4=4-x^2$, so $2x^2=8$, $x=\pm2$. Upper curve is $y=4-x^2$: Area $=\int_{-2}^{2}\left[(4-x^2)-(x^2-4)\right]dx = \int_{-2}^2(8-2x^2)\,dx = \left[8x-\frac{2x^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^2 = \frac{64}{3}$.
questions.explanation: Intersections: $x^2-4=4-x^2$, so $2x^2=8$, $x=\pm2$. Upper curve is $y=4-x^2$: Area $=\int_{-2}^{2}\left[(4-x^2)-(x^2-4)\right]dx = \int_{-2}^2(8-2x^2)\,dx = \left[8x-\frac{2x^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^2 = \frac{64}{3}$.

questions.q: Find the area between $y=x^3$ and $y=x$ on $[0,1]$ (note that $y=x$ is above $y=x^3$ on this interval).
questions.target: More area problems

questions.q: Find the area between $y=x^3$ and $y=x$ on $[-1,1]$ (note the curves cross at $x=0$, so the identity of the upper curve switches).
questions.target: Areas requiring case splits
questions.answer: On $[-1,0]$, $x^3\geq x$; on $[0,1]$, $x\geq x^3$. Area $=\int_{-1}^0(x^3-x)\,dx+\int_0^1(x-x^3)\,dx$. By symmetry both integrals equal $\frac{1}{4}$ (using the earlier result), so total area $=\frac{1}{2}$.
questions.explanation: On $[-1,0]$, $x^3\geq x$; on $[0,1]$, $x\geq x^3$. Area $=\int_{-1}^0(x^3-x)\,dx+\int_0^1(x-x^3)\,dx$. By symmetry both integrals equal $\frac{1}{4}$ (using the earlier result), so total area $=\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.q: Find the area enclosed by $y = x^2$ and $y = 2x - x^2$.
questions.target: Vertical Slices (Integration with Respect to x)
questions.answer: Intersections: $x^2 = 2x - x^2 \Rightarrow 2x^2 - 2x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0, 1$. Top curve is $2x - x^2$. Area $= \int_0^1 (2x - 2x^2)\,dx = [x^2 - \frac{2}{3}x^3]_0^1 = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3$.
questions.explanation: Intersections: $x^2 = 2x - x^2 \Rightarrow 2x^2 - 2x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0, 1$. Top curve is $2x - x^2$. Area $= \int_0^1 (2x - 2x^2)\,dx = [x^2 - \frac{2}{3}x^3]_0^1 = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3$.

questions.q: Find the total area enclosed between $y = \sin x$ and $y = \cos x$ from $x = 0$ to $x = \pi/2$.
questions.target: Crossing Curves and Multiple Regions
questions.answer: Intersection at $x = \pi/4$. On $[0, \pi/4]$, $\cos x \geq \sin x$; on $[\pi/4, \pi/2]$, $\sin x \geq \cos x$. $\int_0^{\pi/4}(\cos x - \sin x)dx + \int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2}(\sin x - \cos x)dx = (\sqrt{2}-1) + (\sqrt{2}-1) = 2\sqrt{2} - 2$.
questions.explanation: Intersection at $x = \pi/4$. On $[0, \pi/4]$, $\cos x \geq \sin x$; on $[\pi/4, \pi/2]$, $\sin x \geq \cos x$. $\int_0^{\pi/4}(\cos x - \sin x)dx + \int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2}(\sin x - \cos x)dx = (\sqrt{2}-1) + (\sqrt{2}-1) = 2\sqrt{2} - 2$.

questions.q: Find the area enclosed between $y = x^3 - x$ and $y = 0$ for $x \in [-1, 1]$.
questions.target: Crossing Curves and Multiple Regions
questions.answer: Due to odd symmetry, integrating directly gives 0 (signed area). Absolute area $= 2\int_0^1 -(x^3 - x)\,dx = 2[\frac{x^2}{2} - \frac{x^4}{4}]_0^1 = 2(1/2 - 1/4) = 2(1/4) = 1/2$.
questions.explanation: Due to odd symmetry, integrating directly gives 0 (signed area). Absolute area $= 2\int_0^1 -(x^3 - x)\,dx = 2[\frac{x^2}{2} - \frac{x^4}{4}]_0^1 = 2(1/2 - 1/4) = 2(1/4) = 1/2$.

questions.q: Find the area enclosed between $y = x^3$ and $y = 4x$.
questions.target: Crossing Curves and Multiple Regions
questions.answer: Intersections: $x^3 = 4x \Rightarrow x(x-2)(x+2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = -2, 0, 2$. By symmetry, total area $= 2\int_0^2 (4x - x^3)\,dx = 2[2x^2 - x^4/4]_0^2 = 2[8 - 4] = 2(4) = 8$.
questions.explanation: Intersections: $x^3 = 4x \Rightarrow x(x-2)(x+2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = -2, 0, 2$. By symmetry, total area $= 2\int_0^2 (4x - x^3)\,dx = 2[2x^2 - x^4/4]_0^2 = 2[8 - 4] = 2(4) = 8$.
